body_text:
Over the base theory ZF, the Axiom of Choice (AC) is equivalent to
a vast constellation of fundamental mathematical principles across
algebra, topology, and analysis. Among the most prominent are:
1. *Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem*: Every set can be endowed
   with a well-ordering.
2. *Zorn's Lemma*: Every non-empty partially ordered set in which
   every chain possesses an upper bound contains at least one
   maximal element.
3. *Right Inverses*: Every surjective function admits a right
   inverse (a section).
4. *Linear Algebra*: Every vector space possesses a Hamel basis.
5. *Topology*: Tychonoff's Theorem, asserting that any product of
   compact topological spaces is compact.

The equivalence of these formulations permits mathematicians to
invoke Choice in whichever structural guise is best suited to the
problem at hand.
